# PQ1 motion & behaviour consistency audit

2026-09-21 · repo at `d9f1468` · **report-only: no file in `pq1/`, `flows/` or `screens/` was changed.**

The design is not the problem — a dozen genuinely good laws survive as roughly two hundred hand-typed copies that agree by luck, which is exactly the part a firmware port cannot inherit. Of 294 findings, 171 change no pixel today; 60 already show on the panel.

**1. A Safe screen can render Ethereum's mark, depending on imports** — The Ethereum mark as the fallback for an icon the device cannot resolve is a design decision, and it stands: "eth" is the schema default, components.glyph falls back to it, and batch-sign already documents it as the intended art. What is NOT covered by that decision is a CORRECT name degrading. components.GLYPHS is filled in waves — 16 names when pq1.components is imported, and `safe` and `cowswap` only when those family packages are, at flows/safe/__init__.py:18 and flows/cowswap/__init__.py:21. So the identical screen dict {"icon": "safe"} renders the Safe mark or the Ethereum mark depending on what happened to be imported first, and the substituted mark ignores the screen's icon_color. The repo already knows: tools/handoff/introspect.py:67-81 exists purely to force-import every family so the generator and the checker do not disagree. Around it sit the genuinely dead parts — resolve_glyph's icon/symbol/monogram branches have no caller — and four prose copies of the legal icon list, three of them incomplete.
  *Highest leverage:* Register every family mark at pq1 import time instead of at family import time (pq1/components.py), so a brand mark can never silently become another brand's; the F-ICON checker rule catches the same class in the repo meanwhile. (S)

**2. Under a real thumb, the input grammar breaks** — The two-button grammar is written per screen instead of once: holding both buttons on a navigation screen runs two independent gestures whose outcome flips with the frame rate (DECLINED at 14 fps, CONFIRMED at 30), a SIGN hold and a DECLINE hold are pixel-identical for the full 2000 ms although the law says the chevrons tell them apart, and the press-down acknowledgment the docs specify — PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS 120, a 4 px chevron nudge — is never drawn, so a 250 ms press gives nothing until release. Transits have the same hole: tap a third screen mid-flight and the morph spring restarts, jumping the glyph from 0.31 to full in one frame; reverse a leg and the text you are returning to keeps fading out for two more frames; press into an entry and nine frames (643 ms) of input are swallowed. It happened because driver.py grew one gesture at a time and flow.py's retarget path was written for the common case, and it costs the one thing a signing device sells: the demo feels certain, the thumb finds it arbitrary.
  *Highest leverage:* pq1/driver.py owns it: one edge table — which edge fires each gesture, what a second button does to a live one, and what a press does to a screen already in flight — so every screen inherits the same answer instead of deciding locally. (M)

**3. The frames you watch hardest are thrown away** — 'A fade, never a cut' holds everywhere except the moments that carry the trust: a token-resting ending drops its caption and resolved dress in a single frame (a 5.7–8.7 whole-frame jump) while everything else rides the alpha spring, the qubit film's first frame turns send's black disc near-white with 2477 pixels differing, the check cuts in at full black on every branded ending because the mark fades by scaling its colour toward black, and the goo bridge is born and dies opaque because an 8 px alpha ramp is computed and then discarded by a `> 0.5` test. Its mirror is the handful of fade-INs that use ease instead of ease_out: at 14 fps an ease-in shows 5 % of the ink on the first frame where ease_out shows 56 %, which is 143 ms of near-black on a PIN row the user has just opened and a nearly black first frame on every page flip. Both come from the same habit — the entrance was treated as the law and everything else as a detail — and both land on the exact frame the device is asking to be believed.
  *Highest leverage:* In pq1/flow.py, make the outgoing screen's own ink — caption, result glyph, resolved dress, confirm band — ride the same outgoing alpha spring every other element already rides, which removes the whole-frame jumps on every token-resting ending in one edit. (M)

**4. Three landings for the one frame that matters** — RESULT_HOLD_MS 2450 is uniform and its anchor is not — films count it from 'the result begins', verdicts from 'the caption has fully landed' — so the readable hold is 1980, 2150 or 2450 ms depending on which screen told you what happened, and a DECLINED is readable 470 ms less than a CANCELED on the same circle. The landing itself runs three grammars: the films fade glyph and caption linearly over 350 ms with a 120 ms caption lag (1.68 frames, so about a third of the time the stagger is not there at all), the verdicts use the ease_out 300 entrance after a 450 ms beat, and the explosion caption is a third; the three led screens then sit at −140, +300 and +590 ms from their lead's last ring. It happened because loading.py and status.py grew as separate families and were never reconciled, and it costs the most trust-bearing instant in the product — the device saying what it did.
  *Highest leverage:* Pick one landing in pq1/loading.py — glyph ease_out over 300, caption one 145 ms stagger behind, RESULT_HOLD_MS counted from caption-complete — and have status.ResolveStatus and the verdict family share the same helper and the same anchor. (M)

**5. Every film is a script with the ending pre-chosen** — Every film in the system is a closed timeline whose outcome is fixed at construction: 93.5 % of the qubit film is pixel-identical for success and failure and the drawing code is indifferent until t6 (5750 ms), yet nothing can latch a real result, and the system's whole answer to 'the work took longer' is a build-time guess in whole orbit turns, written twice and unavailable to the film that actually ships. The edges of a flow are equally unwritten: 57 of 60 endings simply freeze on their last frame — the most common transition in the product and the one rule DESIGN.md never states — Sim hard-codes t = 0 as the moment the first screen appeared, restart() leaves osc_dir behind so the reopened ask sweeps the wrong way, and unlock_batch freezes forever on a looping BATCH SIGNING screen with its token stuck 59 px off-centre and the padlock verdict behind it unreachable. This is demo-shaped thinking, and it is the theme that cannot be ported as-is: on hardware a signature takes as long as it takes.
  *Highest leverage:* Write the two-tier film contract into pq1/DESIGN.md and back it in pq1/loading.py: name the loop region (t_orbit, t5), the 850 ms turn it wraps by, and the outcome latch at t6, so the film can be started at dispatch and told the answer later. (M)

**6. Every beat is justified in frames nobody named** — The panel runs at 14 fps and the frame period is not a number anywhere in the code: '14 fps' and 'one panel frame' appear at a dozen prose sites, and where a module needs the value it re-derives it by halving an accent floor, landing 1.5 % off. Anything that falls below the resulting 71.43 ms grid quietly becomes a different gesture each time it plays — the ±7 px refusal shake gets 2.94 samples per cycle and renders at 3.41, 4.92 or 5.56 px of a true 6.15, PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS 120 is 1.68 frames, the scan traverse 4.55, the scan's fade-out 0.91. Worse, the measuring instrument lies: save_gif truncates the frame delay twice, so every 30 fps preview the owner has signed off plays 11 % fast, and the follower chain is sub-stepped in previews (72.0 px of trail) but not on the panel (63.4 px) — which means some pace judgements in this system were made through a fast clock.
  *Highest leverage:* Put PANEL_FPS = 14, FRAME_MS = 71.4286 and a frames(ms) helper in pq1/motion.py, then re-express every frame-derived value through it and raise the sub-frame ones (120, 325, the 2-cycle shake) to whole frames. (M)

**7. The verdict law is typed out four times** — The verdict entrance is this system's signature and it survives as four hand-copies that agree by careful typing: T_HOLD takes four values (250 / 350 / 400 / 500) of which only 250 carries a stated reason, the quiet beat before the caption is 450 / 200 / 150 / 0, the rest on the arrived sign is 400 / 350 / 300 / 200 / 0 under three different names, and nine of twelve modules already speak a six-phase timeline that the base class and DESIGN.md still describe as four. padlock stretches T_IN across its whole mechanism, zeroes T_WAIT and then re-types the arrival curve three times; ArriveStatus inlines its own copy of a pair DESIGN.md calls 'the one source'. Nineteen of twenty-two verdicts already hold perfectly still before the caption, so the law is real and good — it is simply not inheritable, and the prose still says the icon 'pops in' at seven sites a year after the pop was outlawed.
  *Highest leverage:* Hoist the six phases and the entrance pair into one VerdictPhases mixin in pq1/status.py backed by constants in pq1/motion.py, so verdict.VerdictAnim, ArriveStatus, padlock and the PIN family inherit the law instead of retyping it. (M)

**8. Navigation is seen seven times, written nowhere** — The transit is what a signer watches seven times per transaction and it is the least specified motion in the repo: DESIGN.md's ~700 / ~500 ms describes only the circle's trip, the measured leg is 800–857 ms in demos and 633–643 ms on device, and the 150 ms the incoming text waits is not mentioned at all. Three more laws sit under it, all currently perfect and all unwritten — the six-layer composition stack (the disc draws last because the repo's alpha idiom makes every faded element a lower layer), 304 of 304 screens clearing the disc by at least 7.8 px across the whole ±95 px hero sweep, and siblings in a row never staggering while one-shots radiating from a point always do. The one member out of family is CHEV_STAGGER 250, which is 0.83 of the envelope it delays where every sibling sits at or under 0.34: the PIN row's chevrons are sequenced after the caption, not staggered with it.
  *Highest leverage:* Write the leg anatomy into pq1/DESIGN.md — nine device frames, five channels on one spring, TEXT_IN_DELAY_MS 150, the six-layer stack, the token-less transit — with the two tokens living in pq1/motion.py. (S)

**9. Four ambient voices, four clocks, no shared beat** — Every repeating motion sits on a 5000 ms or a 2000 ms beat and no token names either, so the voices drift against each other: a hero runs its sweep at 5000 and its chevron hint at 3600, which realign only every 90 seconds, and the pulse rings ignore the screen's settle entirely — each ring is born at full 0.4 alpha every 1000 ms, on the absolute clock, still drawing through a transit. A live hold quiets exactly one of the four: the sweep goes home while the hint, the band bob and the rings keep cycling under the user's thumb. The chain is also sub-stepped in previews and not in Sim (~10 px of trail difference between what was approved and what the panel draws), and the 'one full sweep' dwell is really four fifths of one, which is why the idle GIF closes with a 91 px jump. The confirm screen already demonstrates the fix: two voices, one period, disjoint windows.
  *Highest leverage:* In pq1/flow.py, phase every ambient loop from the screen's own settle (Sim.idle_since) and freeze all of them during a transit and under a live hold — the pulse rings are the only voice not already doing it. (M)

**10. The flow grammar lives only in prose, and drifts** — Twenty-eight of thirty flows obey a canonical grammar of which exactly two clauses are enforced, so authors keep it by hand and the drift is invisible until it isn't: 19 of 24 flows name the chain screen NETWORK precisely so the CHAIN check cannot see it, return-to-ask is implemented five ways plus a sixth nobody calls, one flow renamed a SEND screen to AMOUNT to get past the same check, and firmware/update puts its band_chev intro after the ask, which makes the opening ask unreachable by taps on the device. The written half has drifted the other way — two pointers to a transitions.py that no longer exists, PIN prose still describing commit/delete/hold-to-submit, SKILL.md checkpoints stale by 1.7 seconds, eight docstrings describing code that is gone — and unlock_batch, the worked example every doc points at, follows none of the grammar it is supposed to demonstrate. The whole cost of this theme lands on the next author, who is now the firmware developer.
  *Highest leverage:* Put the canonical grammar into flows/__init__.py's validate_screens as real clauses (id vocabulary, hint == commit == not band_chev, the chain screen, the returning ask, the hub law), then delete every prose copy that disagrees. (M)

**11. The vocabulary is complete; nothing imports it** — The system already has names for almost everything and the code retypes them anyway: `alpha <= 0.01` appears at 48 sites in 26 files, the 300 ms text fade is declared nine times and linked four, the 420 ms shake in five modules, 450 typed five times under a name that means three different things depending on the file, and the refusal excursion five times as a per-screen literal. Curves fare the same — ease_out and decel are inlined in burst.py, the PIN scanline is motion.busy_pulse re-derived by hand to within 1e-15, the symmetric bob is hand-rolled twice — and the units drift under one naming convention: inside padlock alone KICK = 10.0 means 5.8 px while OPEN_LIFT = 9.0 means 9.0 px. None of this changes a pixel today; it is roughly two hundred chances for three of them to stop agreeing, and a port that reads a number named for a vertical bob and implements it literally on a horizontal move.
  *Highest leverage:* Create the timing/ink/excursion token block in pq1/motion.py (with ALPHA_FLOOR in pq1/colors.py, the one leaf every drawing site already imports) and have the literals import it — zero pixels change, and the port inherits one header instead of two hundred numbers. (L)

**12. Measured differences nobody can see: leave them** — Thirteen findings survived measurement as real and unseeable, or as decisions the owner has already settled more than once: a 300 ms fade that opens at alpha 0.26 instead of 0, 28.6 ms of sub-frame drift on a dwell timer, four deceleration exponents between 2.4 and 3.0 inherited from separately tuned source art, seven degrees of difference mid-tumble, the PIN label's 3-on/3-off pulse with exactly one screen using it, the seven words for one ending, the CLI's two naming styles, a side entrance no flow reaches. Normalising them would re-type 48 timing values by up to half a frame, re-key shipped ending folders and churn every number the port has to cross-check, for zero visible change. This is the character of the system, and it is the part of the audit the owner should be happiest about.
  *Highest leverage:* Nothing to change — record the thirteen as deliberate in pq1/DESIGN.md's exceptions section with the measurement that justifies each, so the next audit and the port stop re-opening them. (S)

**13. The panel cannot show the bottom of a fade** — Everything in this system is measured in an 8-bit buffer; the NV3007 is RGB565. Below alpha 0.0137 a white element is simply black on the glass, and from there to 0.0294 it is a single pure-green pixel — so every fade-OUT in the system spends exactly one panel frame as a green ghost, and the MONO ramp's farthest follower (#050505, a designed grey) is a green disc on the device. Of the 54 visibility guards in the code, 48 use 0.01 and sit safely below the floor by luck, and exactly one — the pulse ring's 0.02 — sits above it and culls something the panel would still show. Every 300 ms ease-out fade is visually finished at 232 ms.
  *Highest leverage:* Name PANEL_ALPHA_FLOOR (0.0137) and PANEL_NEUTRAL_FLOOR (0.0294) in pq1/colors.py and have every visibility guard test against them instead of a hand-typed literal. (M)

**14. There is a floor for how long, none for how far** — VERDICT_ACCENT_MIN_MS gives every accent a two-frame time floor, and nothing anywhere bounds displacement. Measured at 14 fps: a transit leg peaks at 22 px per frame and then spends ten-plus frames moving under 0.1 px; the blast ring expands 58 px in one frame on a 2.6 px stroke; and the digit reel steps 28.6 px against its own repeating 46.4 px pitch — 62 % of a pitch per frame, the one place in the system where a wagon-wheel reversal is possible. The follower chain is what stops a 96 px token step reading as a cut, and nothing says so.
  *Highest leverage:* Add a displacement ceiling beside the time floor in pq1/motion.py — and a tighter one for repeating art — then trim declared mechanism windows to their moving part (last_attempt's T_ROLL is ~1150 ms of motion inside a 2000 ms declaration). (M)

**15. Two thirds of the library has never been in a flow** — Twelve of the twenty-one registered animations appear in no flow at all, so every flow-level measurement in this audit was taken on nine of them and generalised. Splicing each of the twelve into a minimal flow shows the generalisation does not hold: screens.spec() stamps handoff=True on all 21 but only 14 act on it, the incoming token is stamped as an opaque black disc over a still-lit screen, sig_error's handoff wash registers 140 px from where its icon actually lands, and the family identity never reaches a spliced token because the spec pins it before the family's DEFAULTS are applied.
  *Highest leverage:* Derive handoff from rests_on_token instead of stamping it True for everything, in screens/__init__.py — then the wash only runs where something actually crossfades. (M)

**16. Five screen keys are dropped in silence** — Across all 30 flows only nine flag combinations ever occur, and pages, words, lead and pulse appear on exactly one screen each — so four behaviours rest on a single example and the collisions between them are unexercised rather than resolved. Worse, the grammar fails two ways at once: 'words' on the wrong kind raises, while 'pages' on a hero is accepted and then silently dropped, so a hash the user was meant to read simply vanishes. Unknown-key rejection would cost nothing today: zero of 897 non-status screens carry a key that would newly fail.
  *Highest leverage:* Reject unknown and misplaced keys in pq1/layout.py's normalize_screens — the corpus already passes, so it is a free guarantee. (M)

**17. The spec a port is built from, audited at last — and fixed** — Doc-vs-code drift was checked in the prose but never in handoff/spec/*.json, the machine-readable files a firmware port is actually built from. It flattened the verdict law to four numbers that only two of 23 animations obey, exported a live timing (FADE_MS) as demo-only so the port checker would hard-fail a correct port, exported dead constants as device, dropped nine real geometry tokens including the whole pager, marked six curves as overshooting when only one is a progress curve, and asserted that endings ignore input without ever testing it.
  *Highest leverage:* All twelve are fixed: scope is now computed from a reader census (device / demo / dead / contract / spec-only), the law publishes its own overrides and a per-anim entrance_window_ms, the tolerated exceptions ship as spec/exceptions.toml, and the input-dead claim is now derived from eight gestures actually applied during an ending. (M)

**18. Where motion may go was never written down** — After time and amplitude, the third value family: the numbers that say where things may move. Seven spatial names are dead or unenforced and all of them are published to the port as if they were law — SWEEP_X_MIN/MAX is the swept disc's ink extent computed from a nominal amplitude, not the centre path, and nothing clamps to it. The canvas has three different horizontal centre axes (214, 213.5, 213), the status film carries a second unlinked copy of the grid, and the words grid's fourth row collides with its own optional label by 45 ink pixels.
  *Highest leverage:* Decide what SWEEP_X_MIN/MAX means, derive it from CENTER_X ± (SWEEP_AMP + CIRCLE_R) or delete it, and mark every stated-but-unenforced bound as a contract rather than a value — the spec now does the latter automatically. (M)

## Tokens ready to adopt

Consistencies that already hold but have no name. Naming them changes no pixel.

| token | value | easing | when it applies | owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PANEL_FPS / FRAME_MS / frames(ms)` | 14 fps, 71.4286 ms per frame; floor for any motion or stagger = 2 frames (145 ms) | `n/a — the grid every duration is expressed and checked on` | Every timing value in the system: no beat is authored as a bare number of milliseconds, no motion or stagger may render in fewer than two panel frames, no 'one panel frame' is derived by dividing something else. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `motion.entrance()` | alpha 0 → 1 with a rise 0.97 → 1 over ARRIVE_MS = 300 ms, no overshoot | `ease_out` | Every icon, sign, mark or result glyph arriving on a screen — the single implementation imported by verdict.VerdictAnim, status.ArriveStatus, padlock and the PIN family instead of three inline copies. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `VERDICT_HOLD_MS (with PIN_HOLD_MS)` | 400 ms; the PIN pill family alone holds 250 ms | `ease_out (also the curve of the token → black handoff crossfade over the same span)` | The black hold before a verdict's first ink, and the span over which a flow token crossfades out into it. Never a per-screen choice; a source canvas's own hold becomes rest on the arrived sign, never this. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `CAPTION_BEAT_MS (with PIN_BEAT_MS)` | 450 ms; 200 ms in the PIN family | `none — a still beat, nothing moves in it` | The quiet between the sign arriving (or its mechanism finishing) and the caption appearing. A mechanism's last moving frame never overlaps the caption's first. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `TEXT_FADE_MS + motion.seq_swap` | 300 ms; a swap is 300 out landing on the beat, then 300 in — never a crossfade | `ease_out on both halves` | Any line of text on the panel: result captions, busy captions, confirm-band messages, detail pages, entry labels and hints. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `TEXT_IN_DELAY_MS (the one channel lag)` | 150 ms, floor 145 ms (2 frames) | `n/a — a delay in front of the follower's own ease_out` | Any composed entrance where a furniture channel and a text channel arrive together — on a leg the incoming text trails the circle by it. A separation under two frames is not a stagger and must be removed or raised. | `pq1/motion.py` |
| `RESULT_HOLD_MS (anchored)` | 2450 ms, counted from the moment the caption is fully landed | `n/a` | Every screen that STATES a result — verdicts, status films, led endings. Not loops, not live entries: an entry has no result of its own. | `pq1/status.py` |
| `ALPHA_FLOOR` | 0.01 — ink below 1 % (byte ≤ 2 on white) is not drawn | `n/a` | Every visibility guard in the renderer; replaces 48 hand-typed literals and the 0.02 outlier in components.pulse that truncates the last 5 % of a fade. | `pq1/colors.py` |
| `LOADING_TURN_MS + loop region` | 850 ms per orbit turn; loop = (t_orbit, t5); outcome latch at t6 (5800 ms) | `n/a — constant spin, pixel-exact across the wrap` | Any loading film: it lengthens only in whole turns, may wrap its loop region while real work is outstanding, and takes its outcome no later than t6 instead of at construction. | `pq1/loading.py` |
| `COMPOSITION_STACK + TOKEN_TEXT_CLEARANCE` | 6 px minimum clearance; stack bottom → top: screen canvas · corner chevrons · screen text · follower trail · pulse rings · token disc + hold fill | `n/a` | Every screen layout and every transit frame — the disc draws last because a faded element is always the lower layer, and the layout must keep it off the ink across the whole ±95 px sweep. | `pq1/DESIGN.md (enforced in pq1/layout.py)` |

## If you change five things

1. ANSWER THE PRESS, WITHIN TWO FRAMES, EVERYWHERE. Render PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS at last — raise 120 -> 145 (it is the only motion token below the repo's own two-frame floor) and make it a 4 px chevron displacement along the pointing direction that HOLDS while the button is down, returning on HOLD_SNAPBACK_MS 200 ease_out. An out-and-back sampled once per frame can land on its zero crossing and show nothing. Then close the other two press gaps: land a dialled digit within CHORD_MS 150 on any touched slot (today LEFT takes 250 ms, so -1 is slower than +1 and press-to-digit reaches 386 ms), and stop eating presses for 9 frames on the leg into an entry. Highest leverage because it is the only item on this list an owner can feel.
1. OPACITY IS ease_out, ALWAYS. Convert the five ease fade-ins (PIN row 500 ms, pin_differ pill 250 and dots 200, pin_mismatch dots 200, page_flip's incoming page 300) and the four linear film-resolve ramps (loading.py:102-103, status.py:330-331). At 14 fps a 300 ms fade has four frames and ease spends two of them at or below 9 %; the PIN row is invisible for 143 ms after it is meant to have opened. Reserve ease for geometry and colour that start and stop on screen. Same durations, same end times, one frame sooner to legible everywhere.
1. GIVE THE FRAME A NAME AND PUT EVERYTHING ON IT. Add PANEL_FPS 14, FRAME_MS 71.43 and PREVIEW_FPS 30 (today 14 exists only in prose at twelve sites and two screens derive 'one panel frame' from the accent floor instead), then round every one-shot duration and every period to n x FRAME_MS. No value moves more than half a frame, 14 are already on grid because 500 ms = 7 frames exactly, and the payoff is that one law stops rendering four poses on one screen and five on another purely because of the sub-frame offset the preceding hold left behind.
1. COLLAPSE THE DUPLICATED VALUES AND FIX THE ONE BROKEN ANCHOR. Nine declarations of the 300 ms text fade -> TEXT_FADE_MS; four of the 400 ms hold -> HANDOFF_MS with PIN_HOLD_MS 250 as the single documented tier (retire 350 and 500); five of the 450 ms beat -> VERDICT_BEAT_MS; five of the 420 ms shake -> SHAKE_MS; five unlinked lead-lags -> LAG_MS 150 (which also lifts the film's caption lag off 120 ms / 1.68 frames, where it currently reads as simultaneous). Then make RESULT_HOLD_MS 2450 count from the caption LANDED on films as well as signs, so 'UPDATE DECLINED' stops being readable 470 ms longer than 'SAFE TX DECLINED' on the same cancel circle.
1. ONE BEAT PER SCREEN, AND A PRESS OWNS THE SCREEN. Set CHEV_HINT_PERIOD_MS 3600 -> 5000 so the hero's sweep and hint phase-lock the way the confirm screen's band and bob already do — today they realign only every 90 seconds, which is why the most-seen screen in a transaction looks slightly different each time. And gate the gesture hints on a live hold exactly as the sweep is already gated: today the chevrons can rotate up and bob, and the band can swap, while the commit disc is filling underneath — and the chevrons are the hold's own indicator.

## For the firmware developer

Your frame is 71.43 ms and you will sample every animation exactly once inside it, so the one rule that must survive the port is this: no motion may depend on a sample you might not take. Anything shorter than 145 ms — two frames — can land on its own zero crossing and render nothing at all, which is why the press acknowledgment the spec hands you (PRESS_FEEDBACK_MS 120 = 1.68 frames) must become 145 and must be a displacement that STAYS displaced while the button is down, never an out-and-back. Time every gesture window (TAP_MAX_MS 250, CHORD_MS 150, HOLD_COMMIT_MS 2000) from the button's interrupt edge, never from your frame tick: the reference driver polls per frame and consequently fires the hold a frame late, at 2071 ms, with the fill disc already visibly full for a whole frame — a frame in which a release still snaps back from a complete circle. And treat the millisecond values in motion.json as intent, not as truth on your panel: round each one to a whole number of your frames at build time, because otherwise the sub-frame phase offset — not the law — decides whether the verdict's entrance renders four poses or five.

## Nothing here is fixed yet — and that is on purpose

Every open item is recorded in `tools/check/baseline.toml`, one row per violation, each carrying
its finding id and the reason it is tolerated. `python3 -m tools.check` passes today with those
known exceptions and **fails on anything new**. When you fix one, its row reports `STALE` —
delete it. The list only ever gets shorter.

Port today's behaviour unless a theme above says a fix is planned: the catalog and
`spec/*.json` describe the system as it actually is.
